standfirst: A blind date under a false name, a CEO who takes everything literally, and a second couple who quietly ran off with the show. Twelve episodes, no filler, no third-act separation. These six are the same deal: tropes played at full commitment by people who know exactly how silly it is.

picks.why: The template this was built on. A vain, hyper-competent rich man, the woman who has been managing his life for nine years, and a workplace that treats their relationship as a spectator sport. Same webtoon-bright comedy and the same total absence of jeopardy. Difference: sixteen episodes rather than twelve, and it sags slightly in the middle where this never does.

The best-executed romcom on this list: a fated pair, a devoted male lead, and a comic ensemble that lands every beat. Difference: it has a real emotional undertow and will make you cry at least twice, which Business Proposal never attempts.

Friendship-first romance with a heroine who is allowed to be loud, hungry and unpolished. The same feeling of a show that likes its characters more than its plot. Difference: no rich-CEO fantasy and much lower gloss.

Grown-up office romcom with a publishing house full of people you would happily work with, and a second-lead situation handled kindly. Difference: slower, gentler, and it has an actual career story underneath.

The contract-relationship trope taken seriously: same fake-arrangement setup, played as a study of two anxious adults instead of a comedy. Difference: dry and quiet, so if you were here for the shrieking it is the wrong dial.
Same broad crowd-pleasing register with a bigger family ensemble and better food. Difference: a thriller subplot in the back half that lands much harder than the genre led you to expect.

against.title: Crash Landing on You
against.why: The default romcom pick. It is sixteen long episodes with a war, a bereavement and a genuinely painful separation. If you liked Business Proposal because nothing hurt, this will ambush you.

against.title: True Beauty
against.why: The nearest webtoon-adaptation neighbour, so it is always in the same list. But the love triangle is real and unresolved for hours, and the high-school setting makes the stakes teenage rather than delicious.

against.title: Queen of Tears
against.why: Suggested because of the chaebol setting and the comedy in the first act. Then it turns into a terminal-illness melodrama. Completely different contract with the viewer.
